text:
rachel: heads-up, us-west warm-pool reports sustained p95 increases since 11:10. affected nodes mostly in az-a, looks like a single tenant (tenant-ml-research) running very wide attention configs causing NVSwitch arbitration + high host egress.

infra-bot: [ALERT] us-west/warm-pool: p95 latency > 650ms for 12m (rule: infra.latency.p95)

diego: grabbing telemetry. any signs of cross-az spill or cloud egress throttles?

priya: attaching a short metric clip from 11:12:
```
2026-04-05T11:12:28Z pool=warm us-west node=az-a-12 gpu0 util=93 nvlink=82Gb/s nic_tx=4.2GB/s
2026-04-05T11:12:28Z pool=warm us-west node=az-a-12 gpu1 util=35 nvlink=10Gb/s nic_tx=0.3GB/s
2026-04-05T11:12:28Z pool=warm us-west node=az-a-13 gpu0 util=88 nvlink=78Gb/s nic_tx=3.9GB/s
```

ben: bimodal util again + host tx spikes. tenant-ml-research is on shared-burst and runs heavy model shards that checkpoint to S3 frequently. That's both fabric and host IO pressure.

rachel: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) apply transient QoS lowering for tenant-ml-research (nvlink_share and nic_share), 2) live-migrate their replicas to a less utilized dedicated-pool, 3) enable auto-evict rule if per-tenant nvlink > threshold. Thoughts?

diego: (3) sounds good if we can do it safely. auto-evict to ephemeral-burst with backoff and honor PDBs. We also need a safety valve so evicted tenants don't hammer other pools.

priya: we can compose an apictl action that checks nvlink_util>70Gb/s && nic_tx>2GB/s for 30s then trigger reschedule with --evict-policy=rate-limited. Example: `apictl placement evict --tenant tenant-ml-research --to-pool ephemeral-burst --policy rate-limited --grace 90s`

infra-bot: quota manager: per-tenant nvlink_share override supported. Command: `apictl quota set --tenant tenant-ml-research --nvlink-share 0.4 --nic-share 0.5`

ben: cost note: moving them into dedicated-pool reduces noisy neighbor risk but increases cost ~+28% for that workload. If we rely on QoS alone we risk repeated churn. We should quantify monthly delta before proposing carve-outs.

rachel: short-term: Priya, please apply a conservative nvlink/nic quota for 30m and add an auto-evict rule to trigger if quotas still violated after 5m. Diego, can you prepare a quick cost delta for dedicated vs qos for tenant-ml-research?

diego: on it. toggling quota now:
```
apictl quota set --tenant tenant-ml-research --nvlink-share 0.45 --nic-share 0.5 --auto-revert 30m --reason "temp noise mitigation"
```

infra-bot: user diego invoked quota set for tenant-ml-research (nvlink_share=0.45 nic_share=0.5)

priya: after quota applied p95 dropped from ~710ms to ~320ms within one minute. good. I'll stage an auto-evict policy and gate it behind a fabric asymmetry alert (gpu_util.stddev > 0.28).

ben: Diego put the cost stub in a doc: https://intra.redwood/costs/dedicated-vs-qos/tenant-ml-research. rough ballpark dedicated slice adds $4.8k/month.

rachel: thanks. longer term action items: - add per-tenant nvlink metrics to console (owner: priya), - scheduler fabric-weight RFC (owner: diego), - cost/owner decision for carve-out (owner: infra finance). I'll file incident blurb to #incidents after 1h stable.

diego: note for RFC: consider a hybrid strategy: soft-QoS + fabric-weight scheduling + burst-dedicated as an automated escalation ladder to minimize cost while preserving latency. will draft this week.

priya: auto-evict rule pushed to staging, will only trigger if nvlink>75Gb/s for 60s AND nic_tx>2GB/s AND gpu_util.stddev>0.25. will test on a canary pool tomorrow.

rachel: nice coordination. closing loop after 1h of stable p95 or earlier if it recurs. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
